newsitem.title: USA: MBNA tells holders economic downturns "manageable".
newsitem.headline: MBNA tells holders economic downturns "manageable".

text.p: MBNA Corp Chairman Alfred Lerner told the annual meeting Monday that while the company could not avoid any general economic downturn, "We will be better off than our competitors."
"We think that we will always be able to outperform our competitors. It's very hard work... but it's manageable," Lerner said.
He also said the bank was protected from an increase in interest rates because "All of our liability is floating rate."
Company president Charles Cawley disputed shareholders' criticism about MBNA's college campus marketing and comments that credit card operations may be "a house of cards."

"Despite all the rubble about people filing bankruptcy and not being able to pay their bills" only two percent of MBNA's 20 million cardholders, representing $40.3 billion in managed loans, fail to pay, according to Cawley.
He said MBNA's 3.75 percent chargeoff on its loan balance is the lowest in an industry that recently reported losses as high as 8.5 percent.
"Our business is based on the honesty of human beings," Cawley said and attributed chargeoffs to events like a catastrophic illness or job loss rather than to dishonesty.
"I read all those articles too," Cawley said of recent news stories citing analysts' concerns about rising chargeoff rates.
"And every time I read one of those articles I'd like to go like this to the reporter," he said, slamming his fist into his open palm, like a boxer.
Cawley is credited with taking the credit card subsidiary, MBNA America Bank NA, to second place in the industry since the parent corporation went public in 1990.
In other business, shareholders approved the company's slate of directors and two bonus plans for top management.
Lerner said MBNA had no specific plans at this time to expand UK operations into Europe.
